note: Glint, briefs 056 F and 061 (2026-10-25). LOOK ONLY: no rule, sight or replay reads it. Three things that must read the same under day, evening and night although the play camera's grade is not the same: the crossing heads' state colours, the silhouettes' ink and rim, and the occlusion cut's rim. Phase: LightPhase.Current (Day, Evening, Night); evening is eased by LightPhase.Dusk (0 day .. 1 evening): lerp the colour (linear) and the level between `day` and `evening` by Dusk, night switches whole (as RoadLight does). Every colour below is the value BEFORE the grade, as sRGB hex; the grade is the play camera's own (lens.json gradePlay by day, +evening deltas, light.json night). How the numbers were found: briefs/061/glint/ (grade.py is URP's LutBuilderHdr ColorGrade plus AcesTonemap transcribed from the package in Library/PackageCache; it is not yet calibrated against a captured pixel: the batch's first signal frame is the calibration, see validate.py). Bloom, vignette, SSAO and the 3D LUT's interpolation are NOT modelled: the batch's shots confirm (see `confirm`).

crossing.note: The crossing signal head (brief 061 pick A, Vela's Data/signal-lens.json). A head is in the world, so it goes through ACES, the play grade's saturation x1.37 and the bloom: pushed, red drifts to orange (stop x2.0 untrimmed shows #ff4700, hue 17 against 6) and amber to yellow (clearing x2.0 shows #f9d600, hue 52 against 40), mint to pale. Each state therefore has its own pre-grade colour (`colour`, the trim: red and amber lean toward orange and salmon so the grade lands them on the board's colour) and `level` (the linear multiplier of that colour: _EmissionColor = linear(colour) x level, HDR). `shows` is what the grade makes of it at the head's face centre (model), `target` the board's colour it is fitted to, dE the CIEDE2000 between them. Applies to the rim, the figure and the digits (DK_Signal_Rim, DK_Signal_Atlas), the clock ring (DK_Signal_Ring) and the dot rows (DK_Cross_Light, same colour and level; if the dot rows smear into one bloomed line at night, refit them at 0.8, do not just scale: a lower level alone moves the colour 4 to 7 dE). The beam and the halo (DK_Cross_Beam alpha 0.26, DK_Cross_Halo alpha 0.40, additive) take the state's `colour` too, so the additive wash on cream paving leans amber and red, not yellow and pink. ARRIVING takes STOP's values; the rim's blink (offLevel 0.15) multiplies the level. Level crossfade 0.2 s as Vela's data says.
crossing.tolerance: a level 10 percent off moves a state by at most 3.1 dE (clearing, night); the hue stays within 2 degrees of the board's (4 for amber). A measured face centre more than 6 dE from `target` in the batch's shots: refit with briefs/061/glint/fit.py from the measured pixel, do not nudge by eye.
crossing.amberAgainstGuard: The head's displayed amber (#FFB400, hue 42) against the guard cone's own #f0a020 (hue 37, drawn outside the grade, exact): dE 6.4 by day and at evening, 6.0 at night. The same family on purpose (Sky 2026-10-16: no colour is reserved); they never share a shape or a place: the cone is a flat wedge on the ground on the overlay camera with its own motion, the head a floating coin 2.55 m up carrying a walking figure and numerals. Do not push the head's amber apart by hue: yellower than hue 45 goes to the yellow-white the grade makes of any pushed amber. The red STOP against the cone's #e03a2f: dE 5.2, same reasoning. The three heads against each other: walk and clearing 42 to 43 dE, clearing and stop 37, walk and stop 70 to 72.

dayAsBuilt.note: Vela's untrimmed levels on the board colours (what the data held): dE 6.6 / 12.8 / 5.9 from the board colour by day (mint pale, amber yellow, red orange).

silhouette.note: SilhouettePass draws before the post, so the ink fill and the cream rim go through the same grade as everything else: at the values the contract gives (ink #17302f, cream #f7f4ec) the fill would show #000C12 by day and #000506 at night (dE 11 to 14 from ink; the grade's saturation clips red to 0 and the night grade's teal shadow multiplier crushes what is left), and the rim #D6D4CF (grey: the desaturated cream). So the silhouettes' own light is the grade's, not the scene's: they never depend on the LIGHT (the shader is unlit), but they do depend on the grade, so each phase has its own pre-grade colour that lands on `shows`. `fill` target ink #17302f; `edge` target cream, as near as a plain Color (linear max 1.0, no [HDR]) reaches through ACES: #D9D9D2 by day, #E4DBD1 at evening, #DBDBD5 at night (to reach #EEE8DA the value would be above 1.0: an [HDR] _Edge in the shader, not needed for a rim one pixel wide). Set the material colour as the sRGB hex (a Color property converts to linear in a linear project): the first shot measures the fill, which must show within 8 levels a channel of #17302F in every phase; if it shows lighter (the hex taken as linear shows #00958C by day, #85978C at evening, #9B9F9D at night), pass the colour's .linear instead. Cleaner and heavier, only if the pixel check fails or Sky asks for exactness: draw the silhouettes on an overlay camera after the grade like the signal lines (HostFightLab.SignalCamera) with a person-layer cull and the base depth kept; not asked, not done.

fill.dayNote: by day the grade's saturation clips the red of a dark teal; #002C2D is the nearest the day grade reaches (a hue-true ink needs a negative red)

silhouette.edgeMNote: 0.035 m is 1.35 px at 1080p play zoom and about half intensity after SMAA; 0.045 m holds 1.7 px (3.5 px at 2x). The rim is a line, not a glow: its linear value stays at or under 1.0, so it never feeds the bloom (threshold 1.1 by day, 0.9 at night).

capsule.note: Brief 056 F, the capsule cut's cream rim (Sky keeps it until he sees it in play). As built (lerp the wall to cream #f7f4ec by 0.33 at the middle of the dissolve) the rim is not faint on a dark wall: measured on the displayed frame it lifts a deep teal enamel in shade by +37 L*, a night wall by +58 L*, a shaded stone by +10 and a sunlit stone by -1. A white dotted ring round a hole in dark enamel is decoration. Fix: the rim's cream is scaled by the wall's own lit luminance, so it is what the light on that wall would show at the cut's edge and never a fixed white (code, `rimLit`). Same strength, same cream: shaded stone +9 L*, shaded teal enamel +13, night wall +6, night wall in a lamp pool +13, sunlit stone -1. The shape of the rim (the triangle over the soft band) is unchanged.
capsule.rimFallbackNote: 0.45 gives shade stone +12, shaded teal enamel +17, night lamp pool +16 L*; take it only if the batch's frames show no rim at all in shade. Do not raise it above 0.5.
capsule.shadowNote: With `capsules` on the sun's shadow map is NOT cut: a tower casts its full shadow. The old discs and ghostShadow 0.4 lit the street within 11.2 m of the screen centre (and 2 to 4 m round each person) under a tower that is drawn solid, so a lit disc showed in the middle of its shadow. ghostShadow stays 0.4 for the column dither (capsules off). Through a capsule hole the person stands in the tower's shade where the sun puts them, readable: the shade is soft (lens.json sun.shadowStrength 0.62 by day, 0.75 at evening, the sun fills 38 and 25 percent) and the silhouette draws in any shade. Code in briefs/056 (Glint 2026-10-25).
